patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with long-standing type 2 diabetes, diabetic CKD stage 4, CAD and hypertension who joins in 2015. Course runs through CAP, tertiary hyperparathyroidism with parathyroidectomy, anemia of CKD on darbepoetin, right foot osteomyelitis, LAD stent then inferior STEMI, HFrEF, and a left renal cell carcinoma treated by partial nephrectomy in 2026.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Dabrowski phoned about joining. Moved his care because his old doctor is retiring at the end of the summer. Has a kidney doctor already and wants to keep that group. Gave membership info and set up a new patient slot for 9/16. Release signed over the phone script, faxed form to the prior office for the last 3 years of notes, labs, imaging and immunizations.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: prior primary care
documents.body:
Transfer summary, prior internal medicine office, for Stanley Dabrowski, DOB 03/10/1952.

Problems: Type 2 diabetes since about 1997, on basal insulin. Diabetic kidney disease, stage 4, followed by outside nephrology. Hypertension. Coronary artery disease: treadmill test 2012 abnormal, managed medically, no catheterization; aspirin since. Hyperlipidemia. Osteoarthritis both knees; left knee arthroscopy this spring with an outside orthopedic group. Smoker, about a pack a day.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; lisinopril 10 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with each meal; calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily; acetaminophen 650 mg up to four times daily as needed; aspirin 81 mg daily. Metformin was stopped in 2013 when his kidney function declined.

Allergies: none known.

Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2014, normal, 10-year interval. Td 2012. No pneumococcal vaccine on file.

Last labs in the packet: creatinine in the high 2s, A1c in the high 7s.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
63 y/o retired construction foreman establishing care. Prior PCP retiring. Records from that office reviewed before the visit.

Diabetes: dx around 1997. Was on metformin until 2013, off since the kidneys slipped. Now glargine 24 units at bedtime, no other diabetes meds. Checks fingersticks most mornings, reports 140s-170s, no lows he's noticed.

Kidneys: stage 4 diabetic kidney disease, sees outside nephrology every 6 months or so. They manage the sevelamer and calcitriol. Knows to keep away from ibuprofen and the like.

Heart: CAD on a stress test in 2012, medical management, no cath. No chest pain now. Walks the dog around the block, no limit he's noticed.

BP on lisinopril 10. Lipids on atorvastatin 40.

Knees: both arthritic, L scoped this spring, still sore on stairs. Tylenol helps.

PSH: L knee arthroscopy 2015.
FH: father MI at 62. Mother type 2 diabetes and kidney disease. Paternal uncle lung cancer.
SH: divorced, lives alone in Ludlow, daughter close by. Retired from construction, ran crews as a foreman. Smokes about a pack a day, roughly 40 pack-years, not ready to quit but will think about it. 1-2 beers a week.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 146/88. Wt 94 kg, ht 178 cm. Well appearing, raspy voice. No JVD. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, few scattered expiratory sounds that clear with cough. Abd soft. Ext: no edema, crepitus both knees, no effusion. Feet: skin intact, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP palpable.

A/P
1. Type 2 DM with CKD 4: glargine 24 qhs. A1c, CMP, UACR today.
2. CKD 4: per nephrology. Phosphorus today, will forward.
3. HTN: above goal today, recheck next visit before any change.
4. CAD, stable: aspirin, statin.
5. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today.
6. Tobacco: counseled, precontemplative. Meets criteria for annual low-dose CT; ordered and he agrees.
7. OA knees: acetaminophen.
8. HM: colonoscopy 2014 normal. Hep C and HIV screen today. Flu and pneumococcal at a nurse visit in October.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stanley, your labs are back. Kidney function is in the range your kidney doctor has been following, and the A1c is 7.8, which is reasonable for you. Cholesterol is at goal on the atorvastatin. Hemoglobin is a little low, which goes along with the kidney disease. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. I'll send a copy to nephrology. See you in December.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here per PCP plan from new patient visit. Flu vaccine L deltoid, PPSV23 R deltoid. Screening questions negative. Tolerated, waited 15 min without issue. VIS given.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose non-contrast CT of the chest, baseline screening exam. Lungs: no nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Upper abdomen unremarkable on limited images.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your screening CT shows no lung nodules. We'll repeat it next November. The best thing you can do for your lungs is still to stop smoking; my door is open whenever you want help with that.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 3 mo f/u DM, CKD, HTN. Doing fine. Morning sugars 130-160. No lows. Knees about the same. Still smoking, cut back a little on his own.

O: vitals per flowsheet. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact.

A/P: DM2 with CKD 4 - A1c and BMP today, glargine unchanged. HTN - pressure noted, he prefers to keep the current regimen for now. CAD stable. Next nephrology visit in January. RTC 3-4 mo.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Dabrowski on 1/19/2016 for his diabetic kidney disease, CKD stage 4. He feels well. Creatinine is in his usual range and potassium is acceptable on lisinopril. Phosphorus is controlled on sevelamer with meals; PTH 164 on calcitriol 0.25 mcg, which is fine for his stage. Hemoglobin is mildly reduced and we will follow it.

We reviewed avoiding NSAIDs and holding lisinopril on sick days with vomiting or diarrhea.

Current medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg three times daily with meals, calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up in 6 months.

Nephrology

documents.title: Follow-up

documents.body:
Winter was long, less walking, more snacking by his account. Sugars running a bit higher in the mornings, 150s-180s. No hypoglycemia. Nephrology letter from January reviewed, stable.

Exam: BP and weight per flowsheet. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

Plan: A1c today. Talked about getting back out walking now that the weather is turning. Smoking: still about a pack, not interested in medication. Back in 4 months with fasting lipids and urine.

documents.title: A1c

documents.author: PCP

Fasting today. Back to walking most evenings, a mile or so with the dog. Morning sugars mostly 130s now. Knees ache after yard work, acetaminophen does the job.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema. Feet: no calluses, monofilament intact, pulses palpable.

A/P: DM2 with CKD 4 - labs today incl. A1c, CMP, CBC, UACR, lipids. Copy to nephrology (seeing them later this month). HTN on lisinopril 10. CAD no symptoms. Eye exam due, will book with his optometrist. RTC fall for preventive visit and flu shot.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Dabrowski returned on 7/25/2016. Thank you for forwarding your July labs, which we used in place of a repeat draw. Kidney function is unchanged, CKD stage 4. Albuminuria persists at a level consistent with diabetic nephropathy. Phosphorus and potassium acceptable. No changes to sevelamer or calcitriol.

Blood pressure in our office was mildly above target; continue lisinopril 10 mg, home readings would help.

Return in 6 months.

Nephrology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit, age 64. Feels about the same as last year. Turns 65 in March and has his Medicare paperwork started.

ROS negative except chronic knee ache. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no masses. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin no concerning lesions. Feet intact.

Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2014 normal. Eye exam August, no retinopathy. Flu shot given today. PPSV23 done last fall. Lung screening CT due next month, ordered. Smoking cessation: discussed again, he wants to try cutting down first.

Chronic problems reviewed and stable per recent nephrology note. A1c and BMP today. RTC early winter.

documents.title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Welcome to Medicare visit.

Functional: independent with everything, drives, does his own shopping and cooking. No falls in the past year. Hearing OK in one-on-one conversation, misses some in crowds. Vision corrected, eye exam yearly. Home safety reviewed - has railings, no throw rugs.

Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Advance directive: none; daughter would be his health care proxy, gave him the form to take home.

Exam: per flowsheet, otherwise unchanged from last visit.

Screening ECG today: sinus, no acute change.
Preventive plan written out for him: AAA ultrasound (ordered), annual lung CT in November, flu each fall, PCV13 this fall, shingles vaccine when the new one is available at his pharmacy, colonoscopy not due until 2024, eye exam yearly.

Smoking: advised to quit, he's willing to try nicotine gum on his own. Not ready for a quit date.

reports.text: Limited ultrasound of the abdominal aorta for aneurysm screening. The aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximum diameter 2.1 cm in the infrarenal segment. No focal dilation. Common iliac arteries normal caliber. Both kidneys are small and echogenic, consistent with known chronic kidney disease; no hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: No abdominal aortic aneurysm. Small echogenic kidneys.

Medications unchanged. Allergies: NKDA.

Nephrology

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine service.
Admitted 12/20/2017, discharged 12/24/2017.

Diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe.

Presentation: 65 y/o man with diabetes, CKD stage 4, CAD and hypertension, a current smoker, with two days of fever, productive cough and shortness of breath. On arrival febrile and breathing a little fast but with stable pressures. Chest film showed right lower lobe consolidation.

Course: Treated with IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin for the full stay; afebrile by day 3 and no discharge antibiotic needed. His home glargine was held on admission and he was managed on a hospital regimen of glargine given each morning with sliding-scale correction, glucose checks every 6 hours. On hospital day 3 (12/22), a few hours after the morning glargine, nursing noted his glucose had come down from 228 to 112 mg/dL with no change in his fluids or what he was eating. He was awake and had no symptoms. Exam was otherwise normal and showed no lipodystrophy at injection sites or any sign of an insulin overdose. The team felt the drop reflected the expected action of the insulin dose; no treatment needed and no further drops. Renal function at his baseline throughout.

Discharge medications: resume home regimen unchanged - insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals, calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; repeat chest x-ray in 6-8 weeks. Smoking cessation advised.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 3 days after discharge. Feeling better, cough looser, no fever. Back on his usual glargine at bedtime, morning sugars 120s-150s, no lows. Eating OK. Has all his meds. Discharge summary received today and routed to PCP. Follow-up booked 1/3.
